title: More power from a compact USB-C adapter
takeaway: Compact USB adapters serve different devices and changing demands; this project targets 100 W continuous output with a 65 W continuous minimum. Planning message; the power objectives are visible.

speaker_notes: These adapter examples show the range of power and devices served by USB supplies. The 5 W adapter is a USB power adapter, while the 20 W and 140 W examples use USB-C. The adapter bodies are shown at approximately the same scale; the photographs use different viewing angles. Higher-power devices still need an adapter that is practical to carry and use, so compactness matters alongside power delivery. USB Power Delivery selects an output voltage for the connected device. Demand can also change during operation: a device may be connected after startup, removed, or draw little power while attached. The supply must respond to these changes while maintaining the required output. For this project, the target was 100 W continuous output, with a minimum of 65 W continuous. These are design objectives for the USB-C power supply. Delivering that power in a compact converter makes both component size and heat important.
transition: Higher switching frequency can reduce the size of the passive components, but it also makes switching heat a more demanding problem.
